newsitem.title: USA: Kelley, Williams have Louisiana find.
newsitem.headline: Kelley, Williams have Louisiana find.

text.p: Kelley Oil & Gas Corp said Monday a well being drilled with Williams Production - Gulf Coast Co LP made a discovery in Terrebonne Parish, Louisiana.
The Wylie No. 10 encountered about 116 net feet of hydrocarbon bearing sandstone in three formations, based on analysis of open-hole logs, Kelly Oil said.
Due to mechanical difficulties, only the first and second reservoirs can be completed in the existing well bore.
Kelley said the companies have started the Wylie No. 11 adjacent to the Wylie No. 10 discovery well to penetrate the three reservoirs found and targeted objectives not reached.
The first indicated pay consists of about 13 net feet between 10,067 and 10,389 feet and is a normally pressured reservoir behind the intermediate casing, Kelley Oil said.
The second indicated pay consists of 45 net feet between 10,875 and 10,923 feet and also is a normally pressured reservoir behind the intermediate casing.
The lower indicated pay consists of about 58 net feet between 14,186 and 14,300 feet and is a geo-pressured reservoir below the intermediate casing.
The Wylie No. 10 will be completed following the drilling of the Wylie No. 11, Kelley Oil said.
Kelley and Williams Production each have a 50 percent working interest in the south Louisiana exploration program.
Williams Production - Gulf Coast is part of Williams Cos.
